definitions.explanation: The string of a bow used in archery. In the context of Japanese archery, it refers to the string of a traditional longbow.

examples.japanese: {弓弦|ゆみづる}が{切|き}れたので{新|あたら}しいものに{交換|こうかん}した。
examples.english: The bowstring broke, so I replaced it with a new one.

examples.japanese: {弓道|きゅうどう}の{稽古|けいこ}では、まず{弓弦|ゆみづる}の{張|は}り{方|かた}と{手入|てい}れの{仕方|しかた}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: In kyudo practice, you first learn how to string the bow and how to care for the bowstring.

notes:
A compound of {弓|ゆみ} (bow) and {弦|つる} (string). Also written as {弓弦|ゆみつる} without the voicing, though {弓弦|ゆみづる} is more common. The alternate reading {弓弦|ゆづる} also exists and is used as a personal name.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弓弦|ゆみづる}を{張|は}る: string a bow
- {弓弦|ゆみづる}を{引|ひ}く: draw the bowstring
- {弓弦|ゆみづる}が{切|き}れる: the bowstring breaks
- {弓弦|ゆみづる}の{音|おと}: the sound of the bowstring

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {弦|つる}: string (general term for strings on bows and musical instruments)
- {弓|ゆみ}: bow (the weapon/instrument itself)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In {弓道|きゅうどう} (Japanese archery), the bowstring is traditionally made from plant fibers. The sharp twang of the released {弓弦|ゆみづる} is considered part of the aesthetic of {弓道|きゅうどう}. In folklore, the sound of a bowstring was believed to drive away evil spirits.
